search_method.completeness: No search was truncated. Counts are files-with-matches over whole roots; no head/limit truncation was applied to any counted search.
search_method.positive_control: The identical patterns were run against Soma's own tracked source and returned 9 (surface A), 28 (surface B) and 32 (surface C) matching files. A search returning zero everywhere is only meaningful once it is shown to return non-zero where matches are known to exist.

corrections_during_measurement.detail: The first pass used ripgrep defaults, which honour .gitignore. Re-running with --no-ignore --hidden surfaced a match the first pass had silently skipped. All recorded results come from the unfiltered pass.

Pattern `search_knowledge` matched `re-search_knowledge-store` inside SeedMind's test node ids. All patterns were re-run with word boundaries. This also reduced the surface C control count from 49 to 32, because `public_schema_hash` no longer matched as bare `schema_hash`.

dynamic_evidence.probe_limitation: Every probe above was issued by this controller. A probe in which the controller chooses its own operation cannot be evidence of independent client preference. These probes establish that the surfaces are reachable and how they behave; they do not establish which operation any other client selects.

request_logging_absent.finding: Soma's service log records HTTP lines only, in the form 'POST /mcp HTTP/1.1 200 OK'. Every MCP operation is a POST to the same path, and the operation name is carried in the JSON-RPC body, which is not logged.
request_logging_absent.consequence: Exact MCP operation use cannot be measured from existing authorised evidence. Measuring it would require new persistent request logging, which this gate explicitly forbids.

external_traffic_observed.interpretation: Roughly 98 percent of MCP traffic in the current window arrives from outside this machine through the public tunnel. Source addresses were counted and not recorded, per the gate's privacy rules. The 48 distinct sources are likely tunnel edge nodes rather than 48 clients, so they must not be read as a client count. What this does establish is that external clients are actively and heavily using the server while their operation selection is entirely opaque.
external_traffic_observed.significance: This is the reason no MCP-operation surface in this matrix can be upgraded to proven non-use.

surfaces.producer: soma/knowledge_tools_integration.py, registered on the knowledge_action and knowledge_query gateways

replacement_analysis.reads: search_knowledge, get_knowledge and knowledge_health resolve through _project_knowledge_context and read the same knowledge.sqlite3 catalog and the same 10 canonical records that memory_search, memory_get and memory_health return. Verified by probe, not assumed. The generic reads are therefore a live second read surface over canonical content, not an orphaned path.
replacement_analysis.health_difference: memory_health returns canonical_health, provider_health and retrieval_mode; knowledge_health does not. memory_health is a superset, so it is a replacement for the reads but not a rename of them.
replacement_analysis.writes: This is where the families genuinely diverge. save_knowledge and supersede_knowledge write into runs/knowledge/projects/<project_id>/vault inside the repository runs directory, while memory_save writes into the canonical external vault at D:/SomaMemory. Both share knowledge.sqlite3 and both bind the same project_id.
replacement_analysis.scope_authority: The generic operations take project_id and repo_name directly. The canonical family takes an explicit MemoryScope. The generic write path therefore has no scope authority object at all.
replacement_analysis.divergence_hazard: Because the two write paths share one catalog but two vault roots, a generic write would register a canonical-looking record in the shared catalog whose file lives outside the canonical vault. That is a second memory location under one index. Migration is consequently a data question, not a routing rename. This was established by reading the two context builders and was deliberately not tested, because testing it would require a write into memory.

runtime_trace.observation: runs/knowledge/projects/<project_id>/vault exists and is empty, with a directory mtime of 2026-07-29T03:04:25 recorded before any probe in this lane.
runtime_trace.attribution: MarkdownVault.__init__ creates its root directory unconditionally, and _project_knowledge_context is called from exactly three places, all of which are the six generic operations (save/supersede at line 1031, rebuild at line 1088, search/get/health at line 1432). No other code path can create that directory.
runtime_trace.what_it_proves: At least one of the six generic operations was invoked at least once on this machine.
runtime_trace.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not identify which operation, which controller, or when beyond the directory timestamp. The directory being empty means no generic write ever landed a file, which is consistent with a read operation or with a save that failed before writing. It may also have been created by an owner or Soma lane session on 2026-07-29 rather than by an external client.

surfaces.producer: soma/capabilities.py schema_hash() over PATCH_OPERATION_SCHEMA, emitted through capability_metadata() on every gateway response
surfaces.verified_replacement: public_schema_hash for contract identity, discovery_cache_generation for cache staleness, and per-operation hashes from capability_identity
surfaces.emission_vs_consumption: Every probe in this lane received schema_hash. Emission was never in question and is not evidence of consumption.

consumption_contract_found.finding: schema_hash is not merely emitted. system_query.capability_identity accepts expected_schema_hash as a public input and compares it against the running value, appending the mismatch label 'connector_schema_hash' when they differ.
consumption_contract_found.reachability: The assertion input exists on capability_identity only. The same parameter is rejected on self_check with extra_forbidden, so the comparison surface is narrower than the source-level search suggested.
consumption_contract_found.significance: The mismatch label names the connector explicitly. The field has a designed comparison contract offered to external controllers, whether or not any controller currently uses it.

in_repo_consumers.behaviour: compares source schema against the running process value and reports source_running_schema_hash drift
compares a caller-supplied expected_schema_hash and reports connector_schema_hash drift
declares schema_hash as a required response property, so removing it is a schema change

name_collision_excluded.finding: soma/hermes_companion_client.py, hermes_companion.py and hermes_companion_protocol.py all carry fields named schema_hash and expected_schema_hash, and HermesServiceStart requires expected_schema_hash with min_length=64.
name_collision_excluded.resolution: These are a different field. They are computed by effective_schema_hash() in hermes_companion_protocol.py over Hermes tool definitions, not by capabilities.schema_hash() over PATCH_OPERATION_SCHEMA.
name_collision_excluded.why_recorded: Counted naively, Hermes looks like a mandatory live consumer of the legacy capability field. It is not. Reporting that would have been a false active consumer, and it would have made schema_hash look permanently unretirable for the wrong reason.

external_consumers.consumer: ChatGPT connector and any other live external client
external_consumers.note: A server can see that it emitted the field. It cannot see whether the client compared it. Nothing in the request path records a supplied expected_schema_hash.

residual_blind_spots: Whether any external controller supplies expected_schema_hash is unobservable without request logging.
A client could persist and compare the value entirely on its own side, leaving no server-visible trace at all.
surfaces.migration_requirement: Any deprecation must remove a declared response property from six strict output schemas and remove a public assertion input from capability_identity. That is a public contract change requiring its own gate, independent of consumer evidence.
surfaces.owner_acceptance_required: Not applicable. The recommendation is retention, which requires no acceptance of residual risk.
surfaces.note: This confirms the correction made at the close of LEGACY-RETIREMENT-AUDIT-1. schema_hash is keep_live rather than keep_compatibility_read, and the reason is now measured rather than argued: it has a live comparison path that returns a different result depending on what the caller supplies.

bridge_status.question: Does the Pre-Roadmap V3 bridge now have enough evidence to close?
bridge_status.detail: One of the three blocked questions is now answerable and two are not. Surface B moved from unmeasured to measured-and-empty and can proceed to an owner decision. Surfaces A and C cannot, but for different reasons: A is blocked on observability, while C is no longer blocked on evidence at all and is simply a retention decision.

successor_decisions.scope: A separate, owner-reviewed gate to decide whether Soma should record MCP operation names, and nothing else, for a bounded window. Operation name only: no arguments, no response bodies, no prompts, no addresses, no session identifiers.
successor_decisions.rationale: This is the single missing capability behind surface A. This lane is explicitly forbidden from adding it, and did not.
